Data & Methodology

Calculations use only /app/benchmark/data.csv. Dates are parsed as DD-MM-YY; observations are sorted by date and daily log returns are computed from the close. Annualization uses 252 trading days. The file contains 6,399 rows from 2000-08-30 through 2026-03-03, which extends beyond the 2000–2025 wording in the assignment; this report preserves the full provided dataset rather than truncating or fabricating values.

Volatility regimes are classified from rolling 63-trading-day annualized log-return volatility: low ≤ 33rd percentile (13.58%), medium ≤ 66th percentile (17.19%), high ≤ 90th percentile (24.33%), and crisis > 90th percentile. This quantile method is transparent, reproducible, and robust for a single-asset historical sample.

Return Distribution & Tail Risk

Daily returns show non-normal tail behavior. Excess kurtosis of 7.02 indicates fatter tails than a Gaussian distribution, and the 1% expected shortfall is -4.27% versus a 1% VaR threshold of -3.10%.

  • Tail risk: realized worst daily log return of -12.07% is materially larger than routine volatility would imply.
  • Asymmetry: skewness of -0.47 should be considered when stress-testing gold allocations against liquidity shocks and forced deleveraging episodes.
  • Diversification use: positive full-sample CAGR does not remove the need for drawdown-aware sizing, because large losses cluster in time rather than arriving independently.

Liquidity and Price Movement

Volume is unreliable in the earliest years per the source brief, so volume relationships are evaluated primarily from 2004 onward. Post-2003 correlation between volume and absolute daily return is -0.025; correlation between volume and signed daily return is -0.016. High-volume decile days have average absolute daily log return of 0.89% versus 0.69% for low-volume decile days.

Full-sample average daily volume is 4,283, while average daily volume from 2004 onward is 4,766, a better baseline for liquidity assumptions because early zero-volume observations likely reflect source limitations.

Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Considerations

  • Strategic return profile: gold delivered 12.38% annualized return over the supplied history, but with 17.69% annualized volatility and a -44.36% maximum drawdown.
  • Regime dependence: risk is best managed with regime-aware volatility inputs; the crisis-volatility state captures the top decile of 63-day volatility observations and materially different high-low range behavior.
  • Seasonality: monthly and weekday patterns should be treated as secondary signals because statistical tests do not uniformly support strong standalone calendar effects.
  • Tail management: fat tails and clustered drawdowns argue for stress-test sizing, not just variance-based allocation.
  • Momentum overlay: long-term trend state provides useful context for tactical exposure; current dataset endpoint is constructive relative to the 200-day average.
  • Liquidity assumption: use post-2003 volume statistics for trading-capacity analysis; early zeros should be interpreted as data-quality artifacts rather than genuine market inactivity.
